title: Al-Mudhill, the one who humbles
hook: the one who humbles, who takes away false honor
tomorrow: a woman argues, and a whole surah is named for her. why?

segments.voice: Yesterday, Al-Mu'izz, the Giver of Honor, and its line: honor is his to give. Today, the other hand. What happens when honor is taken back?
screen: `HONOR IS HIS TO GIVE.` → `AND TO TAKE BACK?`

segments.voice: A haul video. Bags lined up across a bed, a car key on a ring, and under it a wall of comments: goals. The Qur'an has a comment section like that. Qarun steps out among his people in all his finery. His treasure is so large, the text says, that its keys alone would weigh down a band of strong men. And the crowd that wants this life says it out loud: if only we had what Qarun has. Then the ground opens. Qarun and his house are gone. The next morning, the people who said if only wake up, and…
screen: `A WALL OF COMMENTS: GOALS.` → `QARUN IN HIS FINERY.` → `THE GROUND OPENS.`

segments.voice: …they say something new. If Allah had not been gracious to us, they say, He would have swallowed us too. The ones who wanted his place now give thanks they never got it. That turn is the work of today's Name: Al-Mudhill, the one who humbles. It sounds harsh, until you hear what Qarun had said when people warned him. I was given all this, he said, because of what I know. A gift he had started calling his own achievement, the way a borrowed jacket starts to feel like yours after a while. Al-Mudhill takes away false honor, the kind you borrowed and forgot was borrowed. In the Qur'an you meet it as a verb, inside a prayer in Surah Al Imran: "Thou exaltest whom Thou wilt and Thou abasest whom Thou wilt. In Thy hand is the good." Look at that last line. Raising and lowering, both in one hand, and that hand holds the good. Qarun had the keys. He never had the hand. Here's the detail to tell a friend tonight: some scholars teach that this Name is best said together with yesterday's, Al-Mu'izz al-Mudhill, so nobody hears only half of it. Status is weather. It rolls in, it moves on. The one who sends it does not.
screen: `THE CROWD GIVES THANKS.` · `IT CAME FROM WHAT I KNOW.` · `IN THY HAND IS THE GOOD.` · `SAY IT AS A PAIR.` · then, large: `STATUS PASSES.`

segments.voice: Grab a pen and a scrap of paper. Write one title you'd love people to use for you: captain, top of the class, the one with all the answers. Read it once, fold it in half, and set it face down. For the sit, rest your hands open on your knees, holding nothing.
screen: `WRITE THE TITLE YOU WANT.` · `FOLD IT. FACE DOWN.` · `HANDS OPEN.`

segments.voice: Al-Mudhill. The one who humbles, who takes back honor that was only ever on loan.
Keep this: status passes, and the one who gives it and takes it back stays. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Muslims learn the Names of Allah from the Qur'an and from the list in Jami' at-Tirmidhi and call on them in du'a; some scholars teach that a Name like al-Mudhill is said together with its pair, al-Mu'izz.

fork.setup: you won the award everyone wanted. at dinner your uncle says, 'all you, kid. you earned every bit.' which reply sits closest to today's Name?
options: 'thanks, i really did. nobody worked harder than me.'
'thanks. i worked for it, and it's still a gift, and it'll pass.'
'it was nothing, honestly. anyone could have won it.'
fork.reveal: Qarun's slip wasn't having wealth; it was calling the gift his own doing. brushing it off misses too. thank people, and hold it lightly.

original.note: Arabic: the one who humbles. some scholars pair it with al-Mu'izz, the Giver of Honor.

trapdoor: what you thought: a scary Name, God putting people down.
what it means: the one who takes away false honor, like Qarun's, so a borrowed gift is seen as a gift again.
what a scholar hears: the Name comes from the verb in 3:26 (tudhillu, thou abasest); some scholars advise saying it as a pair, al-Mu'izz al-Mudhill.
guess: the one who humbles, taking back false honor
the one who keeps the proud rich forever
the one who punishes each mistake at once

chat.says: mural high lasted one day. lost council president to Kayla this morning. do i even go tmrw?
options: Go. The title went to Kayla; the work you cared about is still yours.
Skip it. If Allah lowered you, staying on is fighting His decision.
Go, but remind them you nearly won, so your standing doesn't slip.
chat.meaning: Status passes; the one who gives it stays. Losing a title doesn't end the work, and clinging to rank was Qarun's mistake.
